question: On Passage — Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act (H R 4795)
bill_title: Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act of 2026
plain_language: This bill would bar colleges that take federal student aid from commercial boycotts of Israel, and it would require colleges that take certain foreign-language funds to treat programs in Israel like programs in other countries. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

question: On Passage — No Aid for Ghost Students Act (H R 7892)
bill_title: No Aid for Ghost Students Act of 2026
plain_language: This bill requires the Department of Education to establish an identity fraud detection system for the Free Application for Federal Student Aid. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — PROTECT Kids Act (H R 2616)
bill_title: Stopping Indoctrination and Protecting Kids Act
plain_language: This bill requires public elementary and middle schools, as a condition of receiving certain federal funds for elementary and secondary education, to obtain parental consent before changing a student's gender on school forms or changing a student's sex-based accommodations. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Recommit — PROTECT Kids Act (H R 2616)
bill_title: Stopping Indoctrination and Protecting Kids Act
plain_language: H.R. 2616 (Stopping Indoctrination and Protecting Kids Act) requires public elementary and middle schools, as a condition of receiving certain federal funds for elementary and secondary education, to obtain parental consent before changing a student's gender on school forms or changing a student's sex-based accommodations. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Territorial Student Access to Higher Education Act (H R 6472)
bill_title: Territorial Student Access to Higher Education Act
plain_language: This bill requires public colleges that participate in federal student aid programs to charge no more than in-state tuition to students who live in Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, or the U.S. Virgin Islands and are U.S. nationals. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Pregnant Students’ Rights Act (H R 6359)
plain_language: This bill requires colleges that participate in federal student aid programs to give prospective and enrolled students information on rights and resources for pregnant students to carry a baby to term. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Recommit — Pregnant Students’ Rights Act (H R 6359)
